title: Section 1 — Description and history
description: Signature Mail is a mirror of the mail kind of website: a website where a visitor writes a message, addresses it, and sends it. Mail websites began as plain lists of messages, then grew address books, subjects that say what a message is about, and folders that keep messages in order. This mirror follows the same shape — an address book, a subject, and a composed message — rebuilt with Signature branding and the network's own data.

title: Section 3 — Science proof
description: The science behind this mirror is addressing and validation: a message needs a recipient who can be found and a subject that says what it is about. A real mail system looks the recipient up in an address book, checks the message is complete, and then hands it to a delivery system. This mirror does the first two steps and stops: it looks the name up in its sample address book and checks the subject, then shows the composed message with its verdict.

title: Section 5 — Spec / patent + 3D-print version
description: Spec. The Signature spec for this mirror is a draft specification for a local message composer and checker over a fixed sample address book: the address-book format (name, role), the validation rule from Section 2, the composed-message format, and the no-sending, no-account, no-tracking design. The spec is a draft — ready to file, not filed, not a granted patent.

title: Section 6 — Demonstration programs / working prototypes
description: The demonstration on this page is the message composer. Type a recipient and a subject as 'Recipient | Subject' — for example, 'Rin | Harvest fair' — and press the button. The page checks the recipient against the sample address book, checks the subject is not empty, and shows the composed message with its verdict.

title: Section 7 — Two AIs
description: The website AI of this mirror. It discusses the mirror, helps you compose a message in the field, explains any validation verdict, and routes detailed questions to the website or database AI that owns the subject. It speaks in natural sentences and never claims a message was sent.

title: Section 8 — USE section — use, download, copy
description: Use it: use the message composer at the top of this page. Type a recipient and a subject, press the button, and read the composed message.

title: Section 9 — Sources, codes, and network
description: Sources. The mirror's sample address book is the network's own data, made for this mirror. The validation rule is the mirror's own rule, stated in full in Section 2. Addressing and checking a message is a general concept of the mail kind of website, described here in general terms; no outside source is quoted as the mirror's own method.

title: 1. The Signature Mail website AI
description: The website AI of this mirror. It discusses the mirror, helps you compose a message in the field, explains any validation verdict, and routes detailed questions to the website or database AI that owns the subject. It speaks in natural sentences and never claims a message was sent.

title: 2. The AI version of the mail
description: An AI version of the mail service itself. It takes a recipient and a subject in plain words, composes the message from the mirror's own sample address book, and checks it by the rule in Section 2. It sends nothing, and it says so.

title: The demonstration — Recipient and subject
description: Write the message as 'Recipient | Subject', for example 'Rin | Harvest fair'. The demo checks the recipient against the sample address book and checks that the subject is not empty. The message is composed in the page and nothing is sent anywhere — there is no sending on this page.
